messages.content:
The failing test `org.apache.commons.math.complex.ComplexTest.testTanInf()` is testing the `tan()` method of the `Complex` class.

From the bug report, it seems that there is an issue in the calculation of tangent for "big" numbers. The bug occurs when the `sinh(2a)` and `cosh(2a)` values become infinity, resulting in the method returning `NaN` instead of the expected result of `1.0`.

Looking at the implementation of the `tan()` method in the `Complex` class, we can see that the calculation involves dividing `FastMath.sin(real2)` and `FastMath.sinh(imaginary2)` by the sum of `FastMath.cos(real2)` and `FastMath.cosh(imaginary2)`. If either `FastMath.cosh(imaginary2)` or `FastMath.cos(real2)` reaches infinity, the division will result in `NaN`.

To resolve this issue, proper handling or special case logic needs to be added when the `cosh(2a)` or `cos(2b)` values become infinity.

The bug seems to stem from the calculation in the `tan()` method of the `Complex` class.

Next, I will suggest which methods need to be fixed to address this bug.
`org.apache.commons.math.complex.Complex.tan()`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
